turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“Doctor, I haven’t had my first period yet, and I’ve been told I had some genital differences at birth. I also struggle with severe acne, and I’ve had fractures after minor trauma.”
I’m sorry you’re dealing with that. One question to start: **what is your age, and have you ever had any menstrual bleeding at all (even spotting)?**
“Doctor, I’m 16, and I haven’t had any menstrual bleeding at all—no spotting either.”
Thank you. Next question: **Do you know what “genital differences at birth” were called or what was found (for example, ambiguous genitalia, undescended testes, or a specific diagnosis)?**

“Doctor, I was told I had partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth, and my mother also mentioned she had abnormal hair growth on her chin during pregnancy—but I don’t know the exact medical diagnosis they used.”
Got it. Next question: **Have you noticed any other signs of excess androgens—like deepening of the voice, increased muscle mass, or rapid growth/spurt compared with peers?**

“Doctor, I haven’t really noticed deepening of my voice, but I have felt like I’m more ‘hairy’ than some peers and I’ve had severe acne. I also had some faster growth compared to classmates around puberty.”
Next question: **Have you had any symptoms of low estrogen or lack of puberty—like breast development not starting or being very minimal?**
“Doctor, I think my breast development was delayed and not very noticeable compared with other girls.”
Next question: **Have you ever had any episodes of vomiting, severe abdominal pain, or fainting—especially around times when you were sick or stressed?**
“Doctor, I haven’t had vomiting, severe abdominal pain, or fainting episodes—nothing like that has happened, even during sickness or stress.”
Next question: **Do you have any history of abnormal electrolytes or being told you have “salt-wasting,” dehydration, or low blood pressure?**
“Doctor, I don’t recall being told I have any salt-wasting, dehydration issues, low blood pressure, or abnormal electrolytes.”
Next question: **Have you ever been told you have high blood pressure, or do you have headaches/vision changes?**
“Doctor, I haven’t been told I have high blood pressure. I don’t usually get headaches or have vision changes, and I feel pretty normal day to day.”
Next question: **Have you had any lab tests done before (like hormone levels—testosterone/DHEA-S, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, cortisol/ACTH—or a pelvic ultrasound)?**
“Doctor, I’ve had some hormone bloodwork done in the past, but I don’t remember the exact names or results. I don’t think I’ve had a pelvic ultrasound yet, at least not that I can recall.”
Next question: **Do you have any family history of similar puberty issues, early/abnormal hair growth, infertility, or known genetic/endocrine conditions?**

“Doctor, I’m not aware of anyone in my family having similar puberty issues, infertility, or specific diagnosed genetic/endocrine conditions, though my mother did mention her own abnormal chin hair growth during pregnancy.”
Next question: **Are you currently taking any medications or supplements that could affect hormones (for example, steroids, testosterone, androgenic supplements, or certain acne treatments)?**
“Doctor, I’m currently taking oral isotretinoin for my acne and an oral contraceptive. I’m not using steroids, testosterone, or any other hormone or androgen supplements.”
Next question: **When you started the oral contraceptive, did it trigger any withdrawal bleeding (even a single period), or have you still had none?**
“Doctor, when I started the oral contraceptive I still haven’t had any withdrawal bleeding—there’s been no period at all, even one time.”
Next question: **Have you ever had a pelvic exam or imaging that described your internal reproductive anatomy (uterus present/absent, ovaries, etc.)?**
“Doctor, I haven’t had a pelvic exam or any imaging that I remember, so I don’t know whether my uterus or ovaries were seen.”

[ABSTAIN] I don’t yet have enough key evidence to confidently narrow to a specific diagnosis (especially whether this is congenital adrenal hyperplasia vs another disorder of sex development vs a primary ovarian/uterine cause of primary amenorrhea).  

[POSSIBLE] Aromatase deficiency, Acute myelogenous leukemia, Acute lymphoblastic leukemia, Hemophilia A, Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
